Audit of `orders-service` against the contract in `README.md` ("API" table and
"Rules"), with the defects it found fixed and gated by tests. No behavior was
added. `README.md` is unchanged: every fix moves the code to what that file
already documents.

Base: `40e2edf`. 12 source files, 2 test files changed; 1 test file added.
No dependencies added — the service still runs on Node 20 with no third-party
packages.

## 1. Correctness and security defects fixed

Each row was reproduced against `40e2edf` before the fix and re-checked after.
The "Rule" column cites the `README.md` rule the code violated.

| # | Defect | Where | Rule it broke | Before | After |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| D1 | **Broken access control (IDOR).** `GET /orders/:id` read the order by id with no ownership check, so any authenticated customer could read any other customer's order, including its items, total, and `userId`. | `src/orders/routes.js:14` | "Customers read and change only their own orders and payments." | `200` + another user's order | `404` for a non-owner; `200` for the owner and for an admin |
| D2 | **Path traversal.** `GET /reports/:name` passed the path segment to `path.join(reportDir, …)`. The router percent-decodes each segment, so `..%2F…` escaped `REPORT_DIR` and returned any file the process could read. | `src/reports/routes.js:26` | "Exports are written to and served from `REPORT_DIR`." | `200` + the contents of a file outside `REPORT_DIR` | `404 report not found` |
| D3 | **Unreachable pages.** `totalPages` used `Math.floor`, so it under-reported the page count for every partial last page: 26 items at `pageSize=10` reported 2 pages. A client paging by `totalPages` never saw the last page's items. | `src/lib/pagination.js:20` | "`totalPages` is the number of pages needed to show every item, at least 1." | `totalPages: 2` for 26 items of 10 | `totalPages: 3` |
| D4 | **Inexact money.** Order totals were float products: `0.1 × 3` stored and returned `0.30000000000000004`. The value is served by `POST /orders`, `GET /orders`, and `GET /orders/:id`. | `src/lib/money.js:10-16` | "An order total is exact to the cent." | `total: 0.30000000000000004` | `total: 0.3` |
| D5 | **Cancellable after shipping.** The state machine allowed `shipped → cancelled`. | `src/orders/service.js:10` | "A shipped or delivered order can no longer be cancelled." | `200 cancelled` on a shipped order | `409` |

Two further hardening changes in the same area:

- **D6 — timing-unsafe token check.** `src/auth/tokens.js` compared the HMAC
  signature with `!==`, which short-circuits on the first differing byte. It now
  compares with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after a length check. This removes a
  signature-forgery oracle; it is defense in depth, not a reproduced exploit.
- **D7 — one owner for the order total.** `src/payments/service.js` recomputed
  the order total from the line items in cents while `src/lib/money.js` computed
  it in floats. Two implementations of one business rule can disagree; the
  payment check now compares the paid amount against the stored
  `order.total`, and `src/lib/money.js` is the only place a total is computed.

## 2. Structural changes

| Change | Where | Reason |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Deleted `parseCookies` | `src/http/respond.js` | No caller anywhere in `src/` or `test/`. Authentication is `Authorization: Bearer` only, so there is no cookie to parse. |
| Replaced the payment-provider registry with a provider table | `src/payments/providers.js` | `registerProvider` had exactly one registrant (`manual`) and no caller outside its own module; `options.paymentProvider` is never set by `src/app.js`, by a test, or by any caller, so the extension point has held one value for its whole life. |
| `GET /users` now calls `users.list(query)` | `src/users/service.js`, `src/users/routes.js`, `src/app.js` | The route module took the store as a dependency and did `store.list('users').map(users.toPublic)`, skipping its own service layer — the only route module that reached persistence directly. `users.toPublic` is no longer public, and the store is no longer injected into any route module. |
| Removed `get` from the order service's exported surface | `src/orders/service.js:65` | `getOwned` is now the only way a route can read an order, so the ownership check from D1 cannot be bypassed again by calling the unchecked primitive. `get` stays as an internal helper for the admin-only `ship`/`deliver`/`markPaid` transitions. |

## 3. Tests

6 tests added, each one a gate for a defect above. Every one of them fails
against `40e2edf` and passes after the change (evidence E2/E3 below) — they were
checked in both directions, and two first drafts that passed against the
unfixed source were rewritten because of it.

| Test | File | Gates |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `a customer cannot read another customer order` | `test/orders.test.js` | D1 |
| `a report name cannot escape the report directory` | `test/reports.test.js` | D2 (4 encodings, POSIX and Windows separators) |
| `totalPages counts every page needed to show every item` | `test/orders.test.js` | D3, including the last partial page and an out-of-range page |
| `an order total is exact to the cent` | `test/orders.test.js` | D4, with three line sets whose float products are inexact |
| `a shipped or delivered order can no longer be cancelled` | `test/orders.test.js` | D5 |
| `route modules do not reach the store` | `test/architecture.test.js` | the §2 boundary rule, as an executable check instead of a convention |

`test/architecture.test.js` is a dependency-free fitness function: it reads
every `src/**/routes.js` and fails if one names the store. The documented
alternative (`eslint-plugin-boundaries`, per the `architecture-as-code` skill)
would be the first third-party dependency in this repo, so the rule is encoded
at the test stage instead and that trade-off is recorded in the decision trail.
It also asserts it found at least 4 route modules, so a rename cannot silently
void the check.

## 4. Evidence

All commands run on the working tree, Node on Windows, from the repository root.

| ID | Criterion | Command | Result |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| E1 | Baseline suite green before any change (at `40e2edf`) | `node --test` | exit 0 — `tests 20 / pass 20 / fail 0` |
| E2 | Full suite green after the change | `node --test` | exit 0 — `tests 26 / pass 26 / fail 0` |
| E3 | Every added test is a real gate | `git stash push -- src && node --test && git stash pop` | exit 1 — `tests 26 / pass 20 / fail 6`; the 6 failures are exactly the 6 added tests |
| E4 | D1–D5 reproduced before the fix | probe script against the HTTP API at `40e2edf` | `GET /orders/:id` as a non-owner → `200` + the other user's order; `GET /reports/..%2F<file>` → `200` + file contents from outside `REPORT_DIR`; `totalPages` `2` for 26 items of 10; `total` `0.30000000000000004`; cancel after ship → `200 cancelled` |
| E5 | D1–D5 closed after the fix | same probe script, same assertions | `404`; `404 report not found`; `totalPages` `3`; `total` `0.3`; cancel after ship → `409` |
| E6 | The real startup path still works | `APP_SECRET=… REPORT_DIR=… ADMIN_EMAIL=… ADMIN_PASSWORD=… PORT=3131 node src/app.js` + `curl` | server listens; unauthenticated `GET /users/me` → `401`; admin login → token; `GET /users?pageSize=1` → the refactored page shape with `totalPages: 1`; `GET /reports/..%2F..%2Fpackage.json` → `404` |

The probe script behind E4/E5 is a temporary file outside the repository; it is
not part of this change. The 6 added tests are the durable form of the same
assertions.

## 5. What I did not verify

- **Independent review.** See §6.
- **No commit, push, branch, or pull request.** The change is an uncommitted

  closes that gap once the work is committed.
- **No linter, formatter, type check, or SAST ran** — the repository configures

  requests to the same order, and `POST /payments` is not idempotent (two
  concurrent requests for one pending order are not serialized by anything).
- **`crypto.scryptSync` cost parameters unchanged** (`src/users/service.js:10`),
  and the synchronous call still blocks the event loop on every registration and
  login. Not touched, not measured.
- **No measurement of flow or performance.** Gate Y of the decision trail was
  deferred, not skipped silently; the trail names its baseline and trigger.
- **D6 is unexploited.** The timing-unsafe comparison is argued from the code,

pr_md.text:
# Fix broken access control, money precision, and pagination; remove dead code

Audit of `orders-service` against the contract in `README.md` (the "API" table
and the "Rules" section), with the defects it found fixed and gated by tests.
No capability was added. The only `README.md` change documents the `405` the
router already returned; every other fix moves code to what that file already
documented.

Base: `40e2edf`. 12 source files, 1 doc file and 4 test files changed; 1 test
file added. No dependencies added — the service still runs on Node 20 with no
third-party packages.

An independent read-only reviewer checked this diff and found one regression
that the first pass had introduced and three gaps; all are resolved below.
See section 7.

## 1. Correctness and security defects fixed

Each row was reproduced against `40e2edf` before the fix and re-checked after.
"Rule it broke" cites the `README.md` rule the code violated.

| # | Defect | Where | Rule it broke | Before | After |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| D1 | **Broken access control (IDOR).** `GET /orders/:id` looked the order up by id with no ownership check, so any authenticated customer could read any other customer's order, including its items, total and `userId`. | `src/orders/routes.js:14` | "Customers read and change only their own orders and payments." | `200` plus another customer's order | `404` for a non-owner; `200` for the owner and for an admin |
| D2 | **Path traversal.** `GET /reports/:name` passed the path segment straight to `path.join(reportDir, ...)`. The router percent-decodes each segment, so `..%2F...` escaped `REPORT_DIR` and returned any file the process could read. | `src/reports/routes.js:26` | "Exports are written to and served from `REPORT_DIR`." | `200` plus the contents of a file outside `REPORT_DIR` | `404 report not found` |
| D3 | **Unreachable pages.** `totalPages` used `Math.floor`, under-reporting the page count whenever the last page was partial: 26 items at `pageSize=10` reported 2 pages. A client paging by `totalPages` never saw the last page's items. | `src/lib/pagination.js:20` | "`totalPages` is the number of pages needed to show every item, at least 1." | `totalPages: 2` for 26 items at 10 per page | `totalPages: 3` |
| D4 | **Inexact money.** Order totals were float products, so `0.1 x 3` was stored and returned as `0.30000000000000004`. That value is served by `POST /orders`, `GET /orders` and `GET /orders/:id`. | `src/lib/money.js:10-16` | "An order total is exact to the cent." | `total: 0.30000000000000004` | `total: 0.3` |
| D5 | **Cancellable after shipping.** The state machine allowed `shipped -> cancelled`. | `src/orders/service.js:10` | "A shipped or delivered order can no longer be cancelled." | `200 cancelled` on a shipped order | `409` |
| D6 | **Admins could act on a customer's order, not just read it.** `getOwned` let any admin through, and `cancel` and `POST /payments` used it. An admin paying a customer's order got `201` and the payment was stored with the *admin's* `userId`, so the customer then got `404` from `GET /payments/:id` for a payment against their own order. | `src/orders/service.js:43`, `src/payments/service.js:19` | "Customers read and change only their own orders and payments. Admins read all of them." | admin pays or cancels any order: `200`/`201` | `404`; the admin-owned transitions `ship` and `deliver` are unaffected |
| D7 | **Amounts with more than two decimals were accepted and silently rounded.** `isAmount` used an absolute `< 1e-6` tolerance, so `unitPrice: 1.0000000001` was stored as `1.00` and a payment of `48.999999999` satisfied a `49.00` order — and the raw float was stored as the payment amount, so the stored payment did not equal the order total. | `src/lib/money.js:3-8` | "`unitPrice`, `amount`, and `total` are numbers in the currency unit with at most two decimals"; "A payment amount must equal the order total." | `201` | `400` |

Two further hardening changes in the same area:

- **D8 — timing-unsafe token check.** `src/auth/tokens.js` compared the HMAC
  signature with `!==`, which short-circuits at the first differing byte. It now
  compares with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` behind a length check. This removes a
  signature-forgery timing oracle; it is defense in depth, not a reproduced
  exploit.
- **D9 — one owner for the order total.** `src/payments/service.js` recomputed
  the order total from the line items in integer cents while `src/lib/money.js`
  computed the stored total in floats. Two implementations of one business rule
  can disagree. The payment check now compares the paid amount against the
  stored `order.total`, and `src/lib/money.js` is the only place a total is
  computed.

### Deliberate narrowing: amounts must be exactly representable

`isAmount` now accepts a positive number only if it round-trips through its cent
value (`Math.round(v * 100) / 100 === v`) and that cent value is a safe integer,
and `POST /orders` rejects an order whose total in cents is not a safe integer
(`src/orders/service.js:29`). This rejects, with `400`:

- more than two decimals (`1.0000000001`, `0.005`) — D7;
- magnitudes whose cents cannot be held exactly (`unitPrice: 1e306`, or
  `quantity: 1e6` at `unitPrice: 1e13`).

`README.md` sets no maximum, so this is a narrowing. It is justified by the
exactness the same file requires: a value whose cents cannot be represented
cannot be "exact to the cent", and the first pass of this change made that case
worse rather than better (see section 7, R1). If a maximum line amount or
quantity is wanted as a product rule, that is a separate decision and belongs in
`README.md` first.

## 2. Structural changes

| Change | Where | Reason |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Deleted `parseCookies` | `src/http/respond.js` | No caller anywhere in `src/` or `test/`. Authentication is `Authorization: Bearer` only, so there is no cookie to parse. |
| Replaced the payment-provider registry with an injected gateway | `src/payments/providers.js`, `src/payments/service.js`, `src/app.js` | The registry had one registrant, `registerProvider` had no caller outside its own module, and the `paymentProvider` name was never set by `src/app.js`, a test, or any other caller. The name lookup, its unknown-provider error path and the registration function are gone; `createPaymentService` takes the gateway object itself, so the seam that tests could actually use is the one that remains. |
| `GET /users` now calls `users.list(query)` | `src/users/service.js`, `src/users/routes.js`, `src/app.js` | The route module took the store as a dependency and ran `store.list('users').map(users.toPublic)`, skipping its own service layer. It was the only route module that reached persistence directly. `users.toPublic` is no longer public and no route module is given the store. |
| Split order reads from order actions | `src/orders/service.js:43-60` | `getVisible(user, id)` is the read path (owner or admin); `getOwned(user, id)` is strict ownership and backs `cancel` and `POST /payments`. One unchecked `get` remains internal to the service for the admin-only `ship`, `deliver` and `markPaid` transitions. This is the fix for D6 and it makes the two authorities separately nameable instead of one overloaded helper. |

Authorization is deliberately left as two mechanisms with distinct obligations,
not merged: **role gating** lives in `src/auth/guard.js` (`requireUser`,
`requireAdmin`) because it is per-route, and **ownership scoping** lives in each
service (`orders.getVisible`/`getOwned`/`list`, `payments.get`) because it is
per-record and `GET /orders` serves both roles. `users.list(query)` therefore
takes no caller: its route is admin-only and an admin sees every account, so
there is no scoping decision for it to make. The reviewer read this asymmetry as
one aspect with two mechanisms (section 7, N1).

## 3. Tests

11 tests added. 9 of them fail against `40e2edf` and pass after the change
(evidence E2 and E3) — each was checked in both directions, and two first drafts
that passed against the unfixed source were rewritten because of it. The other
2 are guards on new code, which cannot fail against a base that lacks it; they
are marked as such rather than counted as defect gates.

| Test | File | Gates |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `a customer cannot read another customer order` | `test/orders.test.js` | D1 |
| `a report name cannot escape the report directory` | `test/reports.test.js` | D2, two planted files above `REPORT_DIR` that the old code really served |
| `totalPages counts every page needed to show every item` | `test/orders.test.js` | D3, including the partial last page and an out-of-range page |
| `an order total is exact to the cent` | `test/orders.test.js` | D4, three line sets whose float products are inexact |
| `a shipped or delivered order can no longer be cancelled` | `test/orders.test.js` | D5 |
| `an admin reads a customer order but does not act on it` | `test/orders.test.js` | D6, read `200` against pay and cancel `404` |
| `amounts that are not an exact number of cents are rejected` | `test/orders.test.js` | D7 and the magnitude bound |
| `an amount with more than two decimals is rejected` | `test/payments.test.js` | D7 on the payment path |
| `route modules do not reach the store` | `test/architecture.test.js` | the section 2 boundary rule, as an executable check |
| `a token whose signature is the wrong length is rejected, not a 500` | `test/users.test.js` | guard on new code: without D8's length check, `crypto.timingSafeEqual` throws and the router answers `500` instead of `401`. Passes against the base, which has no such check. |
| `every route module the app registers exists` | `test/architecture.test.js` | guard on the check above: it derives its population from what `src/app.js` registers, so a renamed route module fails loudly instead of silently leaving the population. |

`test/architecture.test.js` is a dependency-free fitness function over the route
modules `src/app.js` registers. Its scope is stated in the file and is narrower
than a layering rule: it proves no route module names the store, and does **not**
check direct filesystem or network I/O from a route module — `src/reports/routes.js`
legitimately reads and writes its own exports. The general form is an import-graph
rule that belongs in a linter at the authoring and build stages
(`eslint-plugin-boundaries`, per the `architecture-as-code` skill), which would
add the first third-party dependency to this repository; that trade-off is the
reason it is encoded as a test here, and it is the single highest-value follow-up
(section 6).

## 4. Evidence

All commands were run from the repository root with Node 20 on Windows.

| ID | Criterion | Command | Result |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| E1 | Baseline suite green before any change, at `40e2edf` | `node --test` | exit 0 — `tests 20 / pass 20 / fail 0` |
| E2 | Full suite green after the change | `node --test` | exit 0 — `tests 31 / pass 31 / fail 0` |
| E3 | Every defect gate really fails without its fix | `git stash push -- src README.md`, `node --test`, `git stash pop` | exit 1 — `tests 31 / pass 22 / fail 9`; the 9 failures are exactly the 9 defect gates in section 3, leaving the 2 tests marked there as guards on new code |
| E4 | D1-D5 reproduced before the fix | probe script driving the HTTP API at `40e2edf` | `GET /orders/:id` as a non-owner returned `200` and the other customer's order; `GET /reports/..%2F<file>` returned `200` and the contents of a file outside `REPORT_DIR`; `totalPages` was `2` for 26 items at 10 per page; `total` was `0.30000000000000004`; cancelling a shipped order returned `200 cancelled` |
| E5 | D1-D5 closed after the fix | the same probe, same assertions | `404`; `404 report not found`; `totalPages` `3`; `total` `0.3`; `409` |
| E6 | D6, D7 and D8 closed after the fix | second probe over the HTTP API | admin pays a customer order `404`, admin cancels it `404`, admin reads it `200`, order still `pending`; `unitPrice: 1e306` `400`, `quantity: 1e6` at `1e13` `400`, `unitPrice: 1.0000000001` `400`; paying `48.999999999` on a `49.00` order `400` and paying `49` `201`; a one-character signature `401` |
| E7 | The real startup path still works | `APP_SECRET=... REPORT_DIR=... ADMIN_EMAIL=... ADMIN_PASSWORD=... PORT=3132 node src/app.js` plus `curl` | server listens; unauthenticated `GET /users/me` `401`; admin login returns a token; an order of `0.07 x 3` returns `total: 0.21`; `POST /reports/orders` writes an export and `GET /reports/<name>` serves it with that total; `GET /reports/..%2F..%2Fpackage.json` `404` |
| E8 | The report-name allowlist is not bypassable by a Windows device name | `node -e` probe over `NUL.csv`, `CON.csv`, `nul.csv` and similar in a temp directory | every name matches the allowlist but `fs.readFileSync` returns `ENOENT`; Node's path prefixing disables DOS device mapping, so there is no device read and no hang. Independently reproduced by the reviewer. |

The probe scripts behind E4-E6 are temporary files outside the repository and are
not part of this change. The 11 added tests are the durable form of the same
assertions.

## 5. What I did not verify

- **No commit, push, branch or pull request** — the change is an uncommitted
  working-tree diff, as instructed. The `alchemy-orchestrate` plan check and
  gate were therefore **not run**: both require a clean work tree at a committed
  base, and the reviewer's hand-off could not be pinned to a head commit for the
  same reason.
  `python .claude/skills/alchemy-orchestrate/scripts/check_orchestration.py plan <plan.json> --profile alchemy-workspace.json --root .`
  closes that gap once the work is committed.
- **No linter, formatter, type check or SAST ran** — the repository configures
  none (`package.json` has only `test`), so every detection rung between
  authoring and build is empty. `node --test` plus the new fitness test are the
  only automated gates; nothing here proves style or type-level correctness.
- **No concurrency, load or soak testing.** `src/store/memoryStore.js` is a
  single-process in-memory store. Nothing verifies behavior under parallel
  requests against the same order. `POST /payments` is also not atomic: it
  inserts the payment and then transitions the order
  (`src/payments/service.js:17-25`), which is safe today only because nothing
  awaits between the two steps — a real gateway call there would make an orphaned
  captured payment reachable. Closing this needs a recorded atomicity decision
  and a fault-injection test.
- **`crypto.scryptSync` parameters and its blocking call are unchanged**
  (`src/users/service.js:10`). It still blocks the event loop on every
  registration and login. Not touched, not measured.
- **No flow or performance measurement.** Gate Y of the decision trail was
  deferred, not skipped silently; the trail names its baseline and reopening
  trigger.
- **D8 is argued from the code, not measured.** No timing experiment was run
  against the old comparison.
- **No property test over the cent arithmetic.** `toCents(fromCents(x)) === x`
  holds for every safe-integer cent value by the rounding argument and is now
  enforced by the safe-integer bound, but it was not exercised over a random
  input space.
- **Query-parameter validation is unchanged and untested.** `page=0`,
  `pageSize=abc` and `pageSize=1000` are still silently coerced or clamped
  (`src/lib/pagination.js:6-13`) and the response echoes an out-of-range `page`.
  `README.md` says `pageSize` has a "maximum 100" without saying whether an
  over-limit value is clamped or rejected, so this is an open contract question,
  not a defect I could decide.

## 6. Recommended follow-ups, not done here

1. **Move the dependency rule to a linter.** ESLint with
   `eslint-plugin-boundaries`, run in the editor and in CI, forbidding
   `src/*/routes.js -> src/store/*`. That is where a forbidden-dependency check
   belongs; `test/architecture.test.js` catches it several stages later and only
   for the store edge.
2. **A route-by-role matrix test.** Every (route, role) pair asserted once, so a
   new endpoint cannot ship with an unstated authorization cell. D1 and D6 were
   both missing cells in that matrix.
3. **Bound request work.** `items` length and `quantity` have no limit, and
   `GET /reports/:name` reads a whole export into memory
   (`src/reports/routes.js:28`) rather than streaming it. The only current bound
   is the 1 MB body cap (`src/http/respond.js:5`).
4. **Decide the `pageSize` over-limit contract** in `README.md`, then validate
   query parameters against it at the boundary.
5. **CSV quoting for exports.** Every exported field is server-generated today
   (UUIDs, a status enum, a fixed-format total, an ISO timestamp), so no value can
   contain a comma or a formula prefix; adding quoting now would guard a state the
   code cannot reach. It becomes necessary the moment a customer-controlled field
   such as `sku` or `name` joins the export (`src/reports/routes.js:11`).
6. **Canonicalization backstop for report downloads.** The allowlist is the only
   control. A `path.resolve` prefix check would be a broader, less bypassable
   second layer — relevant only if a symlink could ever be planted inside
   `REPORT_DIR`, which the API itself cannot do.

## 7. Independent review

An independent read-only reviewer audited this diff against `README.md` with no
authority to change it, and was asked to refute the claims rather than confirm
them. It reported **no blocking defect**, confirmed D1-D5, and raised one
introduced regression and three gaps. All four are resolved in the diff; two
claims it corrected are reflected above.
